heard: Earth appears as a tiny, invisible speck from deep space. Astronomer Carl Sagan pushed for a portrait from 6 billion kilometers away. Engineers feared the sun's glare would destroy the spacecraft's sensitive cameras. They finally relented, letting the probe look back at our home. Our world is just 0.12 of a pixel in the frame. Light from the shot took over five hours to reach us. The entire solar system is invisible without special optics from deep space.
